::: {.callout-note icon="true"}
## Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:

- explain why `SEQN` alone is not the complete cross-cycle merge key;
- validate key completeness before joining;
- confirm key uniqueness in both component datasets;
- identify overlapping non-key column names;
- perform a one-to-one left join;
- confirm that the CBC row count is preserved;
- identify unmatched Demographic records;
- diagnose row multiplication;
- investigate duplicated participant-cycle keys;
- resolve column-name conflicts safely;
- save a merge-validation report.
:::

# Why merge the components?

The CBC files contain laboratory measurements such as:

```text
LBXHGB
```

The Demographic files contain variables such as:

```text
RIAGENDR
SDMVSTRA
SDMVPSU
survey weights
```

To analyze hemoglobin by participant characteristics, the two components must be joined.

The intended relationship is:

```text
one CBC participant-cycle record
matched to
one Demographic participant-cycle record
```

# The correct merge key

The merge key is:

```r
c(
  "survey_cycle",
  "SEQN"
)
```

`SEQN` identifies participants within NHANES releases.

Because this pipeline combines multiple two-year cycles, `survey_cycle` is retained as part of the analytical key.

This protects against accidental cross-cycle matches.

::: {.callout-warning icon="true"}
## Do not join only by `SEQN`

Even when `SEQN` appears unique in the combined data, the pipeline should explicitly retain the cycle context.

The intended composite key is:

```text
survey_cycle + SEQN
```
:::

# Where this lesson fits

You should already have:

```r
cbc_primary_1999_2018
```

and:

```r
demographics_1999_2018
```

The CBC dataset should contain one primary record per participant and survey cycle.

The Demographic dataset should contain one participant-level record per participant and survey cycle.

# Identify overlapping non-key columns

Find columns that appear in both datasets outside the merge key:

```r
overlapping_nonkey_columns <- intersect(
  setdiff(
    names(
      cbc_primary_1999_2018
    ),
    merge_key
  ),
  setdiff(
    names(
      demographics_1999_2018
    ),
    merge_key
  )
)
```

Inspect:

```r
overlapping_nonkey_columns
```

Potential overlaps may include provenance variables such as:

```text
source_dataset_id
source_component
source_file_id
source_exam
analysis_role
```

These columns may have different values in CBC and Demographic sources.

They should not be allowed to receive automatic `.x` and `.y` suffixes without review.

# Identify Demographic records without a CBC match

Run:

```r
demographics_without_cbc_match <-
  demographics_for_merge |>
  dplyr::anti_join(
    cbc_for_merge,
    by =

  )
```

Inspect:

```r
nrow(

)
```

These records are not necessarily errors.

The Demographic component may contain participants who did not have an eligible or available CBC result.

# Perform the merge

Use the CBC dataset as the left-hand dataset:

```r
cbc_demographics_1999_2018 <-
  cbc_for_merge |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    demographics_for_merge,
    by =
      merge_key,
    relationship =
      "one-to-one"
  )
```

The left join preserves all primary CBC records.

The `relationship = "one-to-one"` declaration requires:

- each CBC key to occur at most once;
- each matching Demographic key to occur at most once.

If either assumption is violated, the join stops.

# Summarize match status by survey cycle

Run:

```r
merge_match_summary_by_cycle <-
  cbc_demographics_1999_2018 |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    survey_cycle
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cbc_records =
      dplyr::n(),
    demographic_matches =
      sum(
        demographic_match
      ),
    unmatched_cbc_records =
      sum(
        !demographic_match
      ),
    match_percent =
      100 *
      demographic_matches /
      cbc_records,
    .groups =
      "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    survey_cycle
  )
```

Inspect:

# If the merge does not work

Use this section immediately when:

- the join reports an unexpected relationship;
- the merged row count increases;
- duplicate keys appear;
- required variables receive `.x` and `.y` suffixes;
- many CBC records remain unmatched.

::: {.callout-warning icon="true"}
## Do not remove the relationship check

When `relationship = "one-to-one"` stops the join, it has identified a key-structure problem.

Do not remove the argument merely to force the merge to complete.
:::

## Confirm that you are using the correct key

Inspect:

```r
merge_key
```

Expected:

```text
survey_cycle
SEQN
```

Do not join only by `SEQN`.

## Check CBC duplicates

Run:

```r
cbc_primary_1999_2018 |>
  dplyr::count(
    survey_cycle,
    SEQN,
    name = "occurrences"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    occurrences > 1
  ) |>
  print(
    n = Inf
  )
```

## Check Demographic duplicates

Run:

```r
demographics_1999_2018 |>
  dplyr::count(
    survey_cycle,
    SEQN,
    name = "occurrences"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    occurrences > 1
  ) |>
  print(
    n = Inf
  )
```

## Extract the duplicated CBC records

Create:

```r
cbc_duplicate_records <-
  cbc_primary_1999_2018 |>
  dplyr::semi_join(
    cbc_premerge_duplicate_keys,
    by = c(
      "survey_cycle",
      "SEQN"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    survey_cycle,
    SEQN
  )
```

Inspect provenance:

```r
cbc_duplicate_records |>
  dplyr::select(
    survey_cycle,
    SEQN,
    source_dataset_id,
    source_file_id,
    source_exam,
    analysis_role
  ) |>
  print(
    n = Inf
  )
```

## Check whether the supplementary examination entered the primary CBC stack

Run:

```r
"L25_2_B" %in%
  unique(
    cbc_primary_1999_2018$source_file_id
  )
```

Expected:

```text
[1] FALSE
```

If the result is `TRUE`, return to Lessons 10 and 11.

The second 2001–2002 CBC examination must remain separate from the primary CBC stack.

## Understand row multiplication

Suppose one CBC key occurs twice and the matching Demographic key also occurs twice.

The join may produce:

```text
2 CBC rows × 2 Demographic rows = 4 merged rows
```

This is a many-to-many relationship.

The increased row count is not a harmless formatting issue.

It changes the analytical dataset.

## Compare key counts directly

Run:

```r
cbc_key_counts <-
  cbc_primary_1999_2018 |>
  dplyr::count(
    survey_cycle,
    SEQN,
    name = "cbc_rows"
  )
```

```r
demographic_key_counts <-
  demographics_1999_2018 |>
  dplyr::count(
    survey_cycle,
    SEQN,
    name = "demographic_rows"
  )
```

Join the key counts:

```r
merge_key_relationship_report <-
  dplyr::full_join(
    cbc_key_counts,
    demographic_key_counts,
    by = c(
      "survey_cycle",
      "SEQN"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cbc_rows =
      dplyr::coalesce(
        cbc_rows,
        0L
      ),
    demographic_rows =
      dplyr::coalesce(
        demographic_rows,
        0L
      ),
    expected_join_rows =
      cbc_rows *
        pmax(
          demographic_rows,
          1L
        )
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    dplyr::desc(
      expected_join_rows
    )
  )
```

Inspect problematic keys:

```r
merge_key_relationship_report |>
  dplyr::filter(
    cbc_rows > 1 |
      demographic_rows > 1
  ) |>
  print(
    n = Inf
  )
```

## Do not use `distinct()` automatically

Avoid:

```r
data |>
  dplyr::distinct(
    survey_cycle,
    SEQN,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  )
```

This silently keeps one record and discards the others.

Before removing any record, determine whether the duplicates are:

- exact duplicates;
- repeat examinations;
- supplementary records;
- conflicting observations;
- records from an incorrectly included source.

## Diagnose automatic `.x` and `.y` suffixes

After a join, names such as:

```text
source_file_id.x
source_file_id.y
```

mean that both datasets contained a non-key column with the same name.

Find overlaps:

```r
intersect(
  setdiff(
    names(
      cbc_primary_1999_2018
    ),
    merge_key
  ),
  setdiff(
    names(
      demographics_1999_2018
    ),
    merge_key
  )
)
```

Rename component-specific columns before joining.

Do not leave ambiguous suffixes in the final analytical dataset.

## Diagnose unmatched CBC records

Inspect:

```r
cbc_without_demographic_match |>
  dplyr::count(
    survey_cycle,
    name = "unmatched_records"
  ) |>
  print(
    n = Inf
  )
```

Compare key classes:

```r
class(
  cbc_for_merge$SEQN
)
```

```r
class(
  demographics_for_merge$SEQN
)
```

Compare cycle classes:

```r
class(
  cbc_for_merge$survey_cycle
)
```

```r
class(
  demographics_for_merge$survey_cycle
)
```

Possible causes include:

- different key classes;
- whitespace in a character key;
- an incomplete Demographic source;
- a cycle label mismatch;
- participant ineligibility;
- missing Demographic records;
- an earlier component-combination problem.

## Compare unmatched cycles

Run:

```r
cbc_without_demographic_match |>
  dplyr::count(
    survey_cycle,
    name = "unmatched_cbc_records"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    survey_cycle
  ) |>
  print(
    n = Inf
  )
```

A concentration of unmatched records in one cycle may indicate a source or labelling problem.

## Confirm that the merge is being performed from CBC

The intended structure is:

```r
cbc_for_merge |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    demographics_for_merge,
    by = merge_key,
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  )
```

Reversing the datasets changes which population is preserved.

# Create a merge-validation table

Run:

```r
merge_validation_summary <-
  tibble::tibble(
    check = c(
      "CBC contains complete merge keys",
      "Demographic data contain complete merge keys",
      "CBC composite keys are unique",
      "Demographic composite keys are unique",
      "No unresolved non-key overlaps remain",
      "Merged row count equals CBC row count",
      "Merged composite keys are unique",
      "Required merged variables are present"
    ),
    passed = c(
      nrow(
        cbc_missing_merge_keys
      ) == 0,
      nrow(
        demographic_missing_merge_keys
      ) == 0,
      nrow(
        cbc_premerge_duplicate_keys
      ) == 0,
      nrow(
        demographic_premerge_duplicate_keys
      ) == 0,
      length(
        remaining_overlapping_nonkey_columns
      ) == 0,
      merged_rows ==
        cbc_rows_before_merge,
      nrow(
        merged_duplicate_keys
      ) == 0,
      length(
        missing_required_merged_variables
      ) == 0
    )
  )
```

Inspect:

```r
print(
  merge_validation_summary,
  n = Inf
)
```

Identify failed checks:

```r
failed_merge_checks <-
  merge_validation_summary |>
  dplyr::filter(
    !passed
  )
```

Stop if any fail:

```r
if (
  nrow(
    failed_merge_checks
  ) > 0
) {
  stop(
    "Merge validation failed: ",
    paste(
      failed_merge_checks$check,
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}
```

# Create a merge audit summary

Run:

```r
merge_audit_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  metric = c(
    "CBC rows before merge",
    "Demographic rows before merge",
    "Merged rows",
    "Matched CBC records",
    "Unmatched CBC records",
    "Unused Demographic records",
    "Duplicated merged keys"
  ),
  value = c(
    cbc_rows_before_merge,
    demographic_rows_before_merge,
    merged_rows,
    sum(
      cbc_demographics_1999_2018$demographic_match
    ),
    sum(
      !cbc_demographics_1999_2018$demographic_match
    ),
    nrow(
      demographics_without_cbc_match
    ),
    nrow(
      merged_duplicate_keys
    )
  )
)
```

Inspect:

```r
print(
  merge_audit_summary,
  n = Inf
)
```

# What success looks like

After this lesson, you should have:

```r
cbc_demographics_1999_2018
```

The merged dataset should:

- preserve every primary CBC record;
- contain at most one Demographic match per CBC record;
- retain a unique `survey_cycle + SEQN` key;
- contain CBC and Demographic variables;
- include a match indicator;
- retain component-specific provenance;
- contain no ambiguous `.x` and `.y` suffixes.

# Common mistakes

## Joining only by `SEQN`

Retain the survey-cycle context.

## Ignoring duplicate keys before joining

Duplicate keys can multiply rows.

## Removing `relationship = "one-to-one"`

This hides rather than resolves key-structure problems.

## Accepting `.x` and `.y` suffixes without review

Rename overlapping provenance columns before the join.

## Using an inner join automatically

An inner join removes unmatched CBC records.

The pipeline uses a left join to preserve the primary CBC analytical population.

## Treating every unmatched Demographic record as an error

Some Demographic participants may not have a corresponding CBC result.

## Using `distinct()` as a universal duplicate fix

Repeated keys must be investigated before records are removed.

## Reversing the left join

The left-hand dataset determines which records are preserved.

## Assuming the join is valid because it completes

A join can run successfully and still produce incorrect row counts or relationships.

- [ ] Demographic records without CBC matches were identified.

- [ ] You know how to diagnose row multiplication.
- [ ] You know not to remove the relationship check.
- [ ] You have not run `quarto render`.

# Knowledge check

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Why use `survey_cycle + SEQN` as the key?

The pipeline combines multiple NHANES cycles. Retaining the cycle with the participant identifier makes the cross-cycle analytical key explicit and prevents accidental cross-cycle matching.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Why specify `relationship = "one-to-one"`?

It verifies that each CBC key and each matching Demographic key occur no more than once. The join stops when the intended relationship is violated.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Why use CBC as the left-hand dataset?

The primary analytical population is defined by the validated primary CBC records. A left join preserves those records while adding Demographic information where available.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## What causes row multiplication?

Row multiplication occurs when one or both datasets contain repeated merge keys. Multiple rows on one side can match multiple rows on the other side.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Should `.x` and `.y` suffixes be accepted automatically?

No. They indicate overlapping non-key column names. The meaning of those columns should be reviewed and component-specific variables should be renamed before joining.
:::

- created match indicators and audit summaries;
